package.description: Live battery monitoring for wireless mice, keyboards, headsets and controllers on Windows.

en-US.description: Live battery monitoring for wireless mice, keyboards, headsets and controllers on Windows.
en-US.longDescription: Battery Hub reads the battery level of wireless HID peripherals — mice, keyboards, headsets and game controllers — and shows them on a single dashboard with a per-device indicator in the system tray and low-battery notifications. Devices with no known protocol can be set up through a guided calibration wizard that identifies which byte of the HID report carries the battery level, so support is not limited to a fixed list of models. Runs entirely locally and collects no user data.
en-US.name: Battery Hub
en-US.releaseNotes:
Battery Hub 2.0 is a fresh start: a rebuilt app on a new foundation, with everything from earlier versions included.
Download Battery-Hub-Installer-2.0.0.exe to install. If you already have Battery Hub, it updates to 2.0 by itself.
New
- Each device can have its own low battery alert. Open a device and set Low battery alert to Custom, for example 30% for a headset. Devices left on Default keep using the level in Settings.
- While the installer runs, the third light on the character blinks like a loading light.

Changed
- Built on Electron 45 (up from 33), with the newest build tools and updater. The installer is about 40 MB larger because of this.

What Battery Hub does
- Live battery level for your mice, keyboards, headsets and controllers in one window, the tray and notifications.
- Works with any Bluetooth device that reports its battery to Windows, Xbox and PlayStation controllers, Logitech HID++ devices, Razer devices, and headsets and mice from SteelSeries, HyperX, Corsair, Logitech, Audeze, MCHOSE and VXE.
- Battery history, drain rate and time left for each device.
- Low battery, charging and fully charged alerts.
- Settings > Help checks your install and devices, and you can send a device report if one doesn't work.
Windows SmartScreen may show "Windows protected your PC" because the installer isn't code-signed. Select More info, then Run anyway.
